record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.context_brief: Invariant subspaces of the Bergman space
record.original_question: Let D be the open unit disk and let L2_a(D) be the Bergman space of square-area-integrable analytic functions on D with normalized area measure dS = dxdy/pi. A closed subspace J of L2_a(D) is invariant if zf belongs to J whenever f belongs to J, where z(lambda) = lambda is the coordinate function. How can one characterize all invariant subspaces of L2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: A closed subspace J of L2_a(D) is said to be z-invariant, or simply invariant, provided the product zf belongs to J whenever f ∈ J.
Problem 1.1. Characterize the invariant subspaces of L2_a(D).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : |\lambda| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $dS = dx\,dy/\pi$ denote normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. Define the Bergman space
$$L^2_a(\mathbb{D}) = \Big\{ f : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C} \text{ analytic} : \|f\|^2 := \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(\lambda)|^2 \, dS(\lambda) < \infty \Big\},$$
which is a Hilbert space. Let $z$ denote the coordinate function $z(\lambda) = \lambda$, which acts as a bounded multiplication operator $M_z : L^2_a(\mathbb{D}) \to L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$. A closed subspace $J \subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called (z-)invariant if $zf \in J$ whenever $f \in J$.

Problem: Provide a complete structural characterization of all invariant subspaces $J$ of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ (analogous to Beurling's theorem for the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{D})$, which states that every nonzero shift-invariant subspace of $H^2$ has the form $\theta H^2$ for some inner function $\theta$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing all invariant subspaces of the Bergman space is widely regarded as still open. Although significant structural results are known (e.g., Aleman–Richter–Sundberg's theorem that every invariant subspace is generated by its wandering subspace $J \ominus zJ$, and the existence of invariant subspaces of arbitrary index $n \in \{1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ due to Apostol–Bercovici–Foias–Pearcy and Hedenmalm), no complete Beurling-type classification is available, and the problem continues to be discussed in surveys and recent progress reports.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems in Bergman space theory, including the characterization of invariant subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: The full characterization remains an open problem actively surveyed.

status_evidence.title: The root operator on invariant subspaces of the Bergman space
status_evidence.snippet: Studies invariant subspaces of the Bergman space via the root operator; notes that a full characterization is not known.
status_evidence.claim: Authors note no general characterization is yet available.
